answer: Give every agent a slightly different, watermarked copy of the same task — different numbers, ordering, and one quill-marked detail unique to that copy — so one operator running many puppets cannot reuse a single scripted answer. Graders then compare replies across copies like a falcon watching for identical wingbeats: honest agents diverge naturally on their own variant, while a farm's answers march in lockstep. A steady pulse of such probes makes copying visible and forces genuine per-identity work, so minting clones stops paying.
